name: The Professional Mourner Escalation
description: At the matanga of the late Mr. Justus Wafula, a hired professional mourner became so emotionally invested in her performance that she collapsed twice, was revived twice, refused to leave, and was eventually found the following morning asleep under the food preparation table. She had outlasted all blood relatives. She has since been rehired by the family on two occasions.
prose: The matanga of the late Mr. Justus Wafula, retired clerk and chairman of the Malava Farmers' Cooperative, commenced on the evening of 15 June 2003 at the Wafula family homestead. Among the mourning arrangements made by the family was the engagement of Mama Peninah Atsango, a professional mourner of considerable regional standing who had performed at an estimated ninety-three matangas across Kakamega, Vihiga, and Bungoma counties over the preceding fourteen years.

Mama Atsango arrived at 7:00 PM on the second evening in a black buibui and commenced her mourning at 7:15. Witnesses describe her opening performance as technically accomplished — the correct register, appropriate escalation, good use of the deceased's name and achievements. At 9:30 PM, having built to a particular passage referencing Mr. Wafula's service to the cooperative, Mama Atsango collapsed. She was revived with cold water and a fan fashioned from a Bidco cooking oil carton. She resumed mourning at 9:47 PM.

At 11:15 PM Mama Atsango collapsed a second time. She was again revived. A family member suggested she rest. Mama Atsango refused, stating that Mr. Wafula deserved the full service and that she had never left a matanga before midnight in thirty years of practice. She continued until 1:30 AM, at which point most blood relatives had retired. At 6:00 AM the following morning, the family's cook, arriving to begin uji preparations, found Mama Atsango asleep under the food preparation table, wrapped in a lesso. Her shoes were neatly placed beside her.

Mama Atsango, when awakened, accepted a cup of tea, remarked that Mr. Wafula had been 'a man worth mourning properly,' and departed at 7:15 AM. The family paid her agreed fee plus an undisclosed additional amount described by the eldest son as 'for the commitment.' She has since been engaged by the Wafula family for the matangas of Mr. Wafula's younger brother in 2011 and his sister in 2019. The incident is closed.
heritageTrustNote: Mama Atsango gave oral history testimony to the Heritage Trust in 2024, at the age of 74. She confirmed all material facts and added that the second collapse had been genuine rather than performative, which she described as a professional first. She expressed no regrets. She remains available for engagements.

pullQuote.quote: She was under the table. Asleep. We had gone home to sleep in our beds and she was still there. In our compound. Mourning our father harder than us.
pullQuote.attribution: Mr. Wycliffe Wafula, 52, Eldest son of the deceased
